recordings.text: As you look at a globe, you can see only half of the sphere at one time. Half a sphere is called a hemisphere.

There are two ways to divide the earth into hemispheres. One way is to divide it at the equator. The area between the equator and the North Pole is called the Northern Hemisphere, or the northern half of the earth. The southern half of the earth, between the equator and the South Pole, is called the Southern Hemisphere.
The Northern Hemisphere contains most of the world’s land masses; the Southern Hemisphere contains most of the world’s water.
The other way to divide the earth into hemispheres is to divide it between east and west. The Eastern Hemisphere has more land, and the Western Hemisphere has more water.
The earth’s largest land areas are called continents. The Western Hemisphere has two continents: North America and South America.

All the inhabitants of the Western Hemisphere are descendants of people from the Eastern Hemisphere. This is why the Eastern Hemisphere is often called the Old World and the Western Hemisphere is called the New World.

Geographers have divided the globe with imaginary lines of latitude and longitude. The parallels of latitude are the lines that run east and west around the globe. The equator divides the Northern Hemisphere from the Southern Hemisphere. The Arctic Circle and the Tropic of Cancer are important lines of latitude in the Northern Hemisphere. Important lines of latitude in the Southern Hemisphere are the Antarctic Circle and the Tropic of Capricorn.

The climate of a region is its characteristic weather conditions over a period of many years. These conditions include temperature and precipitation. Unlike weather, which can change from day to day, the climate of an area remains the same for many years.
Three things help determine the climate of a region: its latitude, its distance from an ocean or sea, and its altitude (height above sea level). Latitude is an extremely important factor.

The region between the Tropic of Cancer and the Tropic of Capricorn receives the most sun all year and is called the torrid zone or the Tropics. Torrid means “scorching.” The Tropics are hot most of the time. There are two temperate zones, one between the Tropic of Cancer and the Arctic Circle and the other between the Tropic of Capricorn and the Antarctic Circle. The temperate zones experience the greatest seasonal changes. Temperate means “neither very hot nor very cold.” Between the Arctic Circle and the North Pole and between the Antarctic Circle and the South Pole are the frigid zones. Frigid means “extremely cold.” The frigid zones are cold all year.

You know that the parallels of latitude run east and west. The lines of longitude run north and south and come together at the North Pole and the South Pole. The lines of longitude are also called meridians. The prime meridian runs through the western parts of Europe and Africa. Its starting point goes through Greenwich, England. The meridians are used to measure distance east or west of the prime meridian.

Notice the numbers along the equator on the world map on page 362. These numbers show degrees of longitude. Locate 180° longitude. This longitude line is halfway around the world from Greenwich, England, and the prime meridian (0° longitude). Locate the prime meridian and the 180° longitude line on a world globe. Notice how they form a great circle around the earth from the North Pole to the South Pole and back, separating the world into the Eastern Hemisphere and the Western Hemisphere.
Beginning at the prime meridian, the earth is divided by longitude into time zones. Time zone maps help people to know what time it is in other parts of the world.

The International Date Line runs along part of 180° longitude. The International Date Line is jagged so it will not cut through Asia or the possessions of New Zealand. Every midnight, a new day begins at the International Date Line. An hour later, the earth has rotated enough for the same new day to begin at 165° east longitude. In another hour, the same day begins at 150° east longitude. By the time midnight comes to the prime meridian, it is already 12:00 noon at the International Date Line. On the East Coast of the United States, it is still 7:00 P.M. of the previous day, and on the West Coast it is only 4:00 in the afternoon of the previous day.

Three of the world’s four oceans border the Western Hemisphere: the Pacific Ocean, Atlantic Ocean, and Arctic Ocean. Note the four oceans on the globes to the right.

The three largest oceans come together around the frozen South Pole continent. For many years, geographers did not know that Antarctica is a continent. Until brave explorers studied the area and found land beneath the ice, it was thought to be a frozen ocean like the Arctic. It was called the Antarctic Ocean. Today, the parts of the Atlantic, Pacific, and Indian Oceans closest to Antarctica are sometimes called the Antarctic Ocean.
An island is a landform that is completely surrounded by water.
